The patient-level primary outcome for this objective is pathological Complete Response (pCR), which is binary yes/no, and the study-level endpoint for this outcome is the rate of pCR, i.e. the percentage of patients that achieved pCR=yes.
The patient is assessed at the time of surgery for whether they achieved pCR=yes.
They have to do the surgery in order to obtain the tissue samples on which they do their pCR assessment.
Pathological Complete Response is defined as the absence of any residual invasive cancer on hematoxylin and eosin evaluation of the resected breast specimen and all sampled ipsilateral lymph nodes following completion of neoadjuvant systemic therapy (i.e., ypT0N0 or ypTisN0 in the AJCC staging system for staging solid tumors in the neoadjuvant setting that was described in a 2014 FDA Guidance for Industry).
